title: Faithfulness of base change on power-torsion modules characterises faithful flatness of the quotient map

standard_prerequisites.name: Faithful flatness of a ring map and its equivalence with surjectivity on spectra
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence of conditions (1) and (2).

standard_prerequisites.name: Identification of modules annihilated by I with modules over R/I, and the resulting description of their base change
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the equivalence of (1) with condition (3).

standard_prerequisites.name: Expressibility of a power-torsion module as a colimit of bounded torsion submodules, and commutation of tensor product with colimits
standard_prerequisites.use: Extends faithfulness from the bounded to the power-torsion case, giving (3) implies (4).

core_obligations: Note that if R -> S is flat then R/I^n -> S/I^nS is flat for every n, and conclude that (1) and (2) are equivalent by the faithful flatness criterion (proof lines 24242-24245).

Establish the equivalence of (1) with (3) by identifying annihilated-by-I R-modules with R/I-modules, using that M tensor_R S = M tensor_{R/I} S/IS for such M, together with the easy faithful flatness lemma (proof lines 24246-24252).
Record that (4) implies (3) is immediate (proof line 24253).

Assume (3): use the flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS and the surjection it induces on spectra, which holds because Spec(R/I^n) = Spec(R/I) and similarly for S, to conclude that base change is faithful on modules annihilated by I^n (proof lines 24253-24257).

Write an I-power torsion module M as the union of the submodules M_n annihilated by I^n, and use that tensor product commutes with colimits to conclude that base change is faithful on all I-power torsion modules, giving (3) implies (4) (proof lines 24257-24260).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring map R -> S and an ideal I of R, and establishes the equivalence of four conditions: that the map be flat with R/I -> S/IS faithfully flat; that the map be flat with Spec(S/IS) -> Spec(R/I) surjective; that the map be flat with base change faithful on modules annihilated by I; and that the map be flat with base change faithful on I-power torsion modules (source lines 24226-24239). The proof first notes that flatness of R -> S gives flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS for every n, so (1) and (2) are equivalent by the faithful flatness criterion (proof lines 24242-24245). The equivalence of (1) with (3) follows by identifying I-torsion R-modules with R/I-modules, using the identity M tensor_R S = M tensor_{R/I} S/IS for R-modules M annihilated by I, together with the easy faithful flatness lemma (proof lines 24246-24252). The implication (4) implies (3) is immediate. The substantive direction is (3) implies (4): assuming (3), the proof uses the previously established flatness of R/I^n -> S/I^nS and the induced surjection on spectra, which follows because Spec(R/I^n) = Spec(R/I) and similarly for S, to conclude that base change is faithful on modules annihilated by I^n; since an I-power torsion module is the union of the M_n annihilated by I^n, and tensor product commutes with colimits, faithfulness extends to all I-power torsion modules (proof lines 24253-24260). The non-routine content is the passage from bounded torsion to all power torsion via the colimit description.
